name: A Visual and Thermal Imaging Dataset of Lemon Fruits Following Controlled Hot-Water Treatment
description: This dataset contains visual and thermal image data collected from 140 lemon fruits (Citrus limon) to investigate surface appearance and thermal responses following controlled hot-water treatment. which was maintained consistently across all image files and processing outputs. The specific cultivar of the lemons was not independently verified. It has been developed and annotated in College of Engineering, Nanjing Agricultural University, Nanjing 210031, China, For each lemon, two visual images were acquired from operationally designated V and H views using the main rear camera of an iPhone 16 Pro Max (48 MP; f/1.78). The smartphone was mounted on a tripod at a fixed distance of 18 cm from the fruit. The lemon was placed on printed blue-grid graph paper, with major grid lines spaced 1.0 cm apart to provide a spatial reference. The fruit was repositioned between acquisitions to obtain the second view. the views are designated operationally as V and H rather than being assumed to be perfectly orthogonal. Thermal images were acquired before and after a controlled hot-water treatment. An initial thermal image (T₀) was recorded before treatment. Each lemon was then fully submerged individually in boiling water maintained at approximately °C for 60 s using a mesh holder. After removal from the water, the fruit was blotted dry using a consistent procedure. Thermal images were acquired using a UNI-T UTi165A handheld infrared thermal imager (160 × 120 pixels; NETD: 50 mK; stated accuracy: ±2 °C or ±2%). The thermal camera was mounted at a fixed distance of 15 cm, with emissivity set to 0.95 and the rainbow colour palette selected. Five additional thermal images were recorded immediately after treatment (T₁) and at 1, 2, 3, and 4 min after treatment (T₂–T₅). The dataset consists exclusively of image data and includes multiple representations of the acquired visual and thermal images. These include: - Raw visual images from the V and H views. - Segmented visual images containing the isolated lemon regions. - Corresponding visual image masks. - Raw thermal images acquired at six time points (T₀–T₅). - Thermal images preserved in TIFF format. - Segmented thermal images containing the isolated lemon regions. - Corresponding thermal image masks. In total, 1,120 primary images were acquired from the 140 lemons, comprising 280 visual images (two views per lemon) and 840 thermal images (six time points per lemon). Additional segmented images, masks, and TIFF-format files are provided as processed or preserved versions of the corresponding primary image data. where applicable, view and thermal time-point labels. Sample inclusion or exclusion was based solely on image quality and was independent of any external target or measurement values. The dataset is intended to provide traceable raw and processed visual and thermal image data for lemon imaging, segmentation, thermal-response analysis, and related computer vision or machine learning research.
